title: warp specialization: a persistent GEMM with a split-role pipeline

steps.title: Role split: TMA warp + MMA warp + epilogue warps, one tile per CTA
persistent + TMEM accumulator double buffering: the epilogue overlaps the main loop of the next tile

cases.name: one_tile
cases.purpose: Exactly one tile and one K tile: each barrier between the three roles is used only once, which makes it easiest to find the side that did not arrive.

cases.name: small
cases.purpose: Less than one tile in all three dimensions: TMA fills out-of-bounds elements with zero, expect_tx is still the byte count of the whole box; the write-back must clip out-of-bounds rows and columns.

cases.name: long_k
cases.purpose: A single tile, 16 K tiles: the ring buffer wraps around 4 times; both the producer's empty parity (phase ^ 1 in the first round) and the MMA's full parity must be right.

cases.name: short_k
cases.purpose: 3 K tiles, fewer than the pipeline stages: the producer issues only the K tiles that exist, and the MMA waits only that many times.

cases.name: aligned
cases.purpose: 2 × 2 tiles, fewer than the number of SMs: the persistent grid takes min(number of tiles, number of SMs), and each CTA has only one tile.

cases.name: tail
cases.purpose: Neither M nor N is a multiple of the tile: the second row of CTAs has only 5 valid rows, and the TMA store must clip the other rows.

cases.name: raster
cases.purpose: 11 × 3 tiles (the last column of tiles has only 88 columns), a K tail of 8 columns.

cases.name: persistent
cases.purpose: 31 × 12 = 372 tiles, more than the 148 SMs: some CTAs process 3 tiles, rotating accumulators 0, 1, 0; each tile has 6 K tiles, so the ring buffer position and parity carry over across tiles; the last group has only 7 rows of tiles (the tail of grouped rasterization).

cases.name: random
cases.purpose: Medium-size random data: error of the same order as cuBLAS.

cases.name: square
cases.purpose: Tensor Core throughput: 137 GFLOP, 512 tiles = 3.46 waves, directly comparable with lab 31.

cases.name: wide
cases.purpose: 550 GFLOP, 128 MB of A and B together (more than L2): the tile order decides how many times A and B are read from HBM.

cases.name: flat
cases.purpose: 137 GFLOP but only 16 K tiles per tile: writing the 256 MB of C is of the same order as the main loop, so whether the epilogue overlaps the main loop decides the speed.
